functions.name: iter::accumulate
functions.signature: unknown
functions.description: Function object that produces a lazy running accumulation (prefix reduce) view over a container. It returns an iterable range whose input-iterator yields the first element, then the result of applying a binary accumulator to the running value and each subsequent element. The binary function defaults to std::plus<>; a custom AccumulateFunc can be supplied. This entity is not a plain function but an inline constexpr function object of type iter::impl::AccumulateFn that constructs iter::impl::Accumulator<Container, AccumulateFunc> and supports optional binding of the accumulator function.
requirements: Container must be an iterable range compatible with get_begin/get_end (i.e., supports iteration); its iterator's dereference type must be valid for the accumulator function.

AccumulateFunc must be invocable as f(T, T) where T is the iterator_deref<Container> type (or compatible), and its return type must be movable/copyable into the internal AccumVal (remove_cvref of the invoke result).
Do not dereference the iterator returned by the resulting Accumulator if it equals end(); for empty containers begin() == end().
The produced iterators model std::input_iterator; they are single-pass and should not be relied upon for multi-pass algorithms or for creating multiple independent passes over the same Accumulator.
AccumulateFunc is stored by value (mutable) inside the Accumulator and is invoked for each increment; it should remain valid for the lifetime of the iterators.

functions.description: Function-object adaptor that partitions a container/range into a fixed number of batches. Usage: auto rng = iter::batched(container, num_batches); then iterate: for (auto batch : rng) { for (auto& x : batch) { ... } }. Returns a Batcher that yields approximately even-sized batches of references to the original elements. When num_batches is 0, the resulting range is empty. Notes: batched is an inline constexpr function object; construction of Batcher is enabled via friendship to allow perfect-forwarding of the source container.

the returned Batcher object must outlive all iterators obtained from it
the underlying container must remain alive and not perform operations that invalidate iterators while iterating batches (elements in batches are accessed via stored iterators)
num_batches >= 0; if num_batches == 0, iteration yields no batches; for num_batches > 0, batches are sized approximately size/container_batches using integer division and remainder distribution
callers should treat the iterators produced by the Batcher as input iterators (single-pass)

functions.name: iter::chunked
functions.signature:
template <typename Container>
iter::impl::Chunker<Container> operator()(Container&& container, std::size_t chunk_size) const
functions.description: Function-like adaptor that splits an input range into consecutive chunks of up to chunk_size elements and returns a range of chunk views. Each dereference of the outer iterator yields a lightweight iterable proxy over references to elements in the underlying container. Intended usage: chunked(container, n), or (depending on the library’s pipe support) container | chunked(n). Notes: the iterator for the returned range is single-pass (input-iterator). The chunk object is a proxy that reuses internal storage across increments; do not retain it after advancing the outer iterator. Some details of exact forwarding/copying semantics of the container are unknown because the helper type IterToolFnBindSizeTSecond and IteratorWrapper are not provided here.
requirements: container must be an iterable type compatible with get_begin/get_end (i.e., it must be readable via begin/end producing input-iterators)
chunk_size may be any std::size_t; if 0, the produced range is empty (no chunks are yielded)
Only single-pass iteration is guaranteed for the outer iterator (iterator_category is std::input_iterator_tag); do not assume multi-pass behavior

Do not store references or pointers to the chunk proxy (or its underlying elements vector) after incrementing the outer iterator; the proxy’s internal storage is reused and will be repopulated on each increment
Elements yielded inside each chunk are references to the underlying container’s elements; mutating them (when the container is non-const) mutates the underlying container

Lifetimes: any references obtained from the chunks remain valid only as long as the underlying container (as owned/stored by the Chunker) remains alive; do not use them after the chunked range is destroyed
Error handling: no exceptions or error codes are specified by this interface in this header; behavior on iterator invalidation or concurrent modification is unspecified

This is a composition of starmap and zip; exact iteration semantics (e.g., truncation to shortest, reference/value categories, and lifetime) follow iter::zip and iter::starmap of this library. The operator is also used to enable pipe/bind-first syntax via PipeableAndBindFirst.
requirements: MapFunc must be callable with argument types corresponding to the elements yielded by zip(containers...). Concretely, when a group of elements is produced from the containers, invoking map_func with that group must be well-formed.
MapFunc must be movable (it is passed onward via std::move).
Each Containers parameter must be acceptable to iter::zip; that is, they must be iterable in the sense required by zip (exact iterable requirements follow zip and are not specified here).

Containers are perfectly forwarded; if temporaries are passed, their lifetime must extend through any use of the returned StarMapper to avoid dangling references (lifetime behavior follows zip/starmap).
Return type is a lazy adaptor (StarMapper<...>); callers must iterate it to trigger evaluation. Error handling and end-conditions follow iter::zip and iter::starmap.
Overload and pipe/bind-first behavior may exist via PipeableAndBindFirst<IMapFn>; usage and requirements for those forms follow that utility (not specified here).

functions.name: iter::imap
functions.description: Function object adapter that applies a callable to elements taken in lockstep from multiple input containers. It constructs a zipped view of all containers and forwards it to starmap so that each tuple of zipped elements is expanded into separate arguments to map_func. Supports partial application and pipe syntax via PipeableAndBindFirst (e.g., imap(f)(c1, c2) or (zip of containers) | imap(f)). Returns a lazy iterable view; work occurs upon iteration. Details such as exact iterator/category and length behavior are those of iter::zip and iter::starmap.
requirements: MapFunc must be callable with exactly as many arguments as there are input containers; the argument types must be compatible with the element/reference types yielded from each corresponding container when zipped (inferred from use of starmap(zip(...))).
Each Containers parameter must be an iterable acceptable to iter::zip; all additional preconditions and constraints of iter::zip apply (e.g., iterator validity, lifetime).

All input containers (or ranges/iterables) must remain alive and unmodified in ways that invalidate iterators for the entire duration of iterating the returned StarMapper view (lifetime requirement implied by returning a lazy view over the provided containers).
map_func and containers are forwarded; map_func must be movable into the returned view (implied by std::move(map_func)).
Error handling, exception guarantees, and length truncation semantics are determined by iter::zip and iter::starmap; callers must consult those components for any additional requirements.

functions.name: iter::powerset
functions.signature: inline constexpr impl::PowersetFn powerset
functions.description: Function-object (callable) that constructs a powerset adaptor over a container. The resulting adaptor iterates all combinations of the input container from size 0 up to the full size (i.e., the mathematical power set, emitted as a sequence of combination-views). Iteration advances through all k-combinations for k=0,1,...,N, internally using combinations(container, k). The adaptor stores the container (by move/copy) and yields lazy sub-iterables for each combination-length. Exact operator() template and return type are defined by IterToolFn<Powersetter> (not visible here); conceptually, calling powerset(c) returns a impl::Powersetter<ContainerLike> that can be range-for iterated.
requirements: Argument must be a container/range that is valid to pass to combinations(container, k) for all k in [0, size].
The size of the container must be determinable via dumb_size(container) (either via a constant-time size or by iteration).
Elements and/or the container must satisfy whatever move/copy requirements combinations(...) imposes; the adaptor stores the container internally (constructed as Powersetter(Container&&)).
The returned adaptor provides input-iterator semantics; consumers should not assume multi-pass or random access.

Iterating requires the underlying container remain in a valid state for the lifetime of the adaptor; the adaptor owns its stored copy/move of the container so external lifetime is not required after construction.

functions.signature:
template <typename T>
constexpr iter::impl::Range<T> iter::range(T stop) noexcept;
functions.description: Creates a half-open range [0, stop) with step 1 for values of type T. Use it to iterate from zero up to but not including stop. Returns a Range<T> that can be used in range-based for loops and supports iteration via its nested Iterator.

requirements: T must be constructible from integer literal 1 (used for step).
T must support comparison (<, <=, >=), addition, and increment by step during iteration.
For unsigned T, elements are produced while value < stop. For signed T, iteration advances by +1 until value >= stop.

Range<T>::size() is not available for floating-point T (static_assert).

In stubs here, FUZZ_PARAM_STR provides this data, which is consumed as raw bytes to build numeric vectors or strings without format requirements.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# We generate an arbitrary binary blob that the stubs interpret as raw bytes via FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# Goals:
# - Sometimes empty, sometimes small, sometimes medium blobs (but <= 4096 bytes total).
# - Include diverse byte patterns to exercise branches: 0x00, 0xFF, increasing, decreasing,
#   repeated runs, alternating patterns, and embedded 32-bit words for sorted/combinations stubs.
# - Keep first few bytes useful as small vectors and strings; mix in sections aligned to 4 bytes.
# - Occasionally embed ASCII text to serve as valid string-y data for adapters that tolerate text.

MAX_SIZE = 4096


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _pattern_zeroes(n: int) -> bytes:
    return b"\x00" * n


def _pattern_ffs(n: int) -> bytes:
    return b"\xff" * n


def _pattern_inc(n: int, start: int = 0) -> bytes:
    return bytes(((start + i) & 0xFF) for i in range(n))


def _pattern_alt(n: int, a: int = 0x00, b: int = 0xFF) -> bytes:
    arr = bytearray()
    for i in range(n):
        arr.append(a if (i % 2 == 0) else b)
    return bytes(arr)


def _embed_u32_le(values: List[int]) -> bytes:
    # pack list of unsigned 32-bit ints little-endian
    return b"".join(struct.pack("<I", v & 0xFFFFFFFF) for v in values)


def _make_sections(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    sections: List[bytes] = []

    # Header: a compact selector segment that multiple stubs may consume for parameters
    header_len = rng.randrange(8, 32)
    header = _rand_bytes(rng, header_len)
    sections.append(header)

    # Small numeric vector-friendly region: 0..255 ramp and small signed values
    small_len = rng.randrange(16, 64)
    small = _pattern_inc(small_len, start=rng.randrange(0, 256))
    sections.append(small)

    # Alternating bits region
    alt_len = rng.randrange(16, 64)
    sections.append(_pattern_alt(alt_len, a=0x00, b=0xFF))

    # Repeated 0xFFs then 0x00s to trigger truthy/falsey filters
    rep_len = rng.randrange(8, 48)
    sections.append(_pattern_ffs(rep_len))
    sections.append(_pattern_zeroes(rep_len))

    # Embed some 32-bit words for sorted/combinations stubs that memcpy uint32_t
    words_cnt = rng.randrange(4, 32)
    words = [rng.getrandbits(32) for _ in range(words_cnt)]
    sections.append(_embed_u32_le(words))

    # ASCII-ish segment with repeats to encourage grouping/unique behavior
    ascii_base = (
        b"Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, amet amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. "
        b"AAABBBCCCDDDEEE   000111222333444555666777888999!!!???\n"
    )
    # Take a random slice and repeat
    start = rng.randrange(0, max(1, len(ascii_base) - 16))
    slen = rng.randrange(16, min(64, len(ascii_base) - start))
    ascii_seg = (ascii_base[start:start + slen]) * rng.randrange(1, 4)
    sections.append(ascii_seg)

    # Another random region to add entropy
    rand_len = rng.randrange(32, 128)
    sections.append(_rand_bytes(rng, rand_len))

    # Optionally prepend/append short control bytes that some stubs mod by small numbers
    ctl = bytes([rng.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(rng.randrange(4, 16))])
    sections.insert(0, ctl)
    tail_ctl = bytes([rng.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(rng.randrange(4, 16))])
    sections.append(tail_ctl)

    return sections


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide an overall target size bucket
    bucket = rng.randrange(0, 6)
    if bucket == 0:
        target = rng.randrange(0, 33)  # possibly empty to hit empty-container paths
    elif bucket == 1:
        target = rng.randrange(33, 128)
    elif bucket == 2:
        target = rng.randrange(128, 512)
    elif bucket == 3:
        target = rng.randrange(512, 1024)
    elif bucket == 4:
        target = rng.randrange(1024, 2048)
    else:
        target = rng.randrange(2048, min(4096, 3072))

    # Build diverse sections
    sections = _make_sections(rng)

    blob = b"".join(sections)

    # Trim or pad to target size
    if len(blob) > target:
        blob = blob[:target]
    elif len(blob) < target:
        # pad with a mix of zeros and randoms to land on the target length
        pad_needed = target - len(blob)
        # Half zeros, half random
        half = pad_needed // 2
        pad = _pattern_zeroes(half) + _rand_bytes(rng, pad_needed - half)
        blob += pad

    # Ensure total size constraint
    if len(blob) > MAX_SIZE:
        blob = blob[:MAX_SIZE]

    return blob
